text: The Patriots' loss to Jacksonville was as ugly as the 35-6 final score suggests, with Drake Maye turning the ball over three times (two interceptions and a lost fumble) in what he himself called an "unacceptable" offensive performance, prompting beat writers to dig into film breakdowns of what went wrong for the quarterback and whether the team is deploying him correctly in the first place. Maye's struggles continued a troubling early-season trend, and the quarterback is clearly looking inward for answers even as questions mount about the Patriots' offensive scheme and his own play, while Jacksonville's Trevor Lawrence torched New England with three touchdown passes in a dominant showing. The few bright spots were sparse—Marcus Jones notched his first interception of the season—but they were overshadowed by the comprehensive nature of the defeat and the deeper concerns about how the offense is functioning around its young quarterback. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the loss in his Monday press conference, though the real conversation among beat writers centers on whether the Patriots need to fundamentally rethink how they're using Maye as he works through this rough patch.
